title: Signal Gnome Pocket Brief & Probe Queue — Apr 2026
summary: Small, concentrated synthesis of recent customer threads about runtime hiccups, KV-cache misses, and routing fallbacks — assembled into a lightweight probe queue for 2-week spikes. Purpose: give eng/sre a short prioritized set of low-effort experiments and a few hypothesis-driven patches to validate impact quickly.
notes_raw: Notes to self / chopping-block: customers call out (1) sudden token-cost jumps when fallback models kick in, (2) KV cache thrash with repetitive chat flows, (3) per-route latency spikes during autoscale events. Many threads include partial repros and stack snippets. This doc distills repeat motifs + quick probes. Contains choppy vignettes below — not polished. TODO: attach raw transcripts to RDW-3382.
customer_vignettes: Fintech startup: observed 2x token cost when hosted fallback used after a holiday burst; customer noticed no obvious quality change but cost increased — wants explicit control over fallback budget.
Healthcare SaaS: KV cache misses when users re-open long context sessions; observed ~120ms extra per-request during rehydration windows; workaround was to reduce max_history but that degrades UX.
E-comm analytics: routing to cheaper quantized variant occasionally increased hallucination rates on invoice extraction; team disabled automatic fallback overnight to avoid regressions.
Marketplace (enterprise): burst autoscale correlated with 20% tail-latency increases for short queries (<64 tokens) due to small-batch inefficiencies on GPU cold-starts.
prioritized_requests: 1) Expose 'fallback-cost-cap' per-route so CS can set a hard budget for model downgrades (low product work, blocked by config surface).
2) Small probe to instrument KV-cache hit/miss ratios at token-prefix granularity for top 10 customers (needs lightweight telemetry + sampling).
3) Investigate tiny-batch cold-start path: add warm-start micro-binning for short queries to avoid small-batch latency cliff (SRE spike).
4) Add model-variant quality smoke test on fallback path (auto-eval on representative prompt set) before enabling automatic fallback for tenant.
quick_probes: A. Fallback budget toggle (2 engineers, 2 days): config flag per-route that sets a token-cost throttle; gated to canary customers.
B. KV-cache sampling hook (1 engineer, 3 days): record prefix length and hit/miss; sample 0.5% traffic, push to ephemeral metrics dashboard.
C. Micro-warm bins (SRE + infra, 1 week): pre-allocate tiny warm pools for <64 token requests during burst windows; measure tail-latency before/after.
D. Fallback canary with eval (product + applied-ml, 3 days): run N prompts through candidate fallback variant and compare embedding/LM metrics; block on quality delta > X.
engineering_risks: Telemetry cost: fine-grain KV-cache sampling may increase observability spend if not capped.
Complexity of per-route budget: surface area risk and potential for surprising behavior if budgets are set too low (may drop to very cheap models).
'Warm bin' memory pressure on nodes if too many micro pools are active; needs cap and eviction policy.
impact_estimates: Rough numbers from earlier postmortems: fixing warm-start small-batch path could reduce P95 by ~15-25% for short queries on heavy tenants; KV-cache probe expected to reveal a 8-12% avoidable token-surge in top 20% noisy workloads; fallback budget prevents obvious bill spikes (savings variable).
